title: MELLO GHETTO HELLO CAPRICE

production_notes: TRACK: 'Mello Ghetto Hello Caprice' -- the instrumental for NIGHT SUN: 77 bars written + 16 held free = 93 bars of rap.

FRONT LINE (his order): Paganini violin, grand piano, harmonica. Ultra Detroit Bounce rhythm sections; a 144-tempo hi-hat flow. SPARSE REALIZATION (the re-strike ruling below): the violin plays a simple memorable REPEATING melody, not virtuoso figuration; the harmonica answers in short phrases, sparingly; the groove wins every contest for the prompt's budget.

WIND LAW (his sanction): if wind is necessary use bagpipes -- the only sanctioned wind voice. No flutes, no breathy pads. (This sparse strike needs no wind beyond the harmonica's short phrases; the pipes stand unspent.)

FEATURE TERRITORY (his ruling): the last verse and outro stay open for the Lady of the Lake, Lakeyah herself -- bars 55-77 sit back, pocket wide open, no dense lead line crowding the last-verse region; the program closes on an open outro vamp (bounce + pocket), not a composed finale.
BAR MAP: Verse I bars 1-27; Verse II bars 28-54; FEATURE (Lakeyah) bars 55-77; his 16 at bars 78-93; then the open outro.

SIGMA (his order): binaural in the 13-31 Hz band that dances with the melody and harmonizes with synergy in the pocket -- struck mode DRIFT over the doctrine pair 200/213 at -28 dB; measured in the manifest.

EAR VERDICT ON PROOF No. 5 'TAKE TWO' (2026-11-09, the only court): FAIL -- 'Still too Frankensteinish not got a flow at all just random instruments with random notes.' Desk reading on record: MusicGen-small improvises locally and never develops; whole-performance generation stands 2-for-2 at modest briefs (the Proven Road: 'Sounds like real instruments this time') and 0-for-1 at density.

RE-STRIKE RULING (his order, 2026-11-09): 'Cut it -- re-strike the Caprice sparse, Proven Road density.' The dense v7 build was cut mid-render and is VOID, unsalvaged, its audio nowhere in this run. This strike (v8) carries FEW simultaneous demands and lets the groove repeat and develop slowly -- repetition is the point; the rap carries the busy-ness. Fallback chained by his order: 'If that fails then the other method' -- the desk sequences the fallback; this run is the sparse attempt only.

notes: performance: ONE invariant prompt, struck once as a seed take and extended only by audio continuation -- the model plays through every join. The takes are spliced DIRECTLY: no crossfade, no per-take RMS matching (there are no sections to match), no grid, no trim, no tempo surgery of any kind.

absent by design: any spine, any kit or sample, any synthesized voice, any second prompt, and any composed arpeggio layer. The Sigma ground is NOT absent in this run: the founder ordered it into the track's spec (the Caprice clause) and it stands measured in the sigma block from the stem as struck.

tempo: the performance chose its own clock. The prompt asked for energy and bounce, never a number; realized tempo stands measured -- globally and per 30 s window -- in the performance block. Drift is reported, not corrected.
the performance itself is not transcribed in composition.abc: its transcription is a separate production, owed and marked owed -- never fabricated.
loudness is K-weighted integrated, UNGATED (BS.1770 gating omitted in the proof build, stated not hidden).
2 s tail fade + 5 ms head fade applied before mastering.

nothing rides: there is NO composed arpeggio layer in this run. The Paganini line stands in the prompt itself, and the performance played its own violin arpeggios as part of its body -- in tune, in phrase, or not at all; the ear will judge what the prompt bought. composition.abc notates nothing and marks the performance's transcription owed.

single session: the whole chain was born in ONE bridge process; every continuation was conditioned on the bridge's in-memory predecessor; no take was resumed from disk, and the session guard verified the chain before the splice. Voided attempts set aside before this strike: 1 (void-attempt-1).

warm-up: 1 leading take(s) (29.94 s) were struck and DISCARDED -- their audio is nowhere in the program. The warm-up's own measured tempo was 71.8 BPM; the kept program's windows stand in the performance block for the lock-in question.
